intro: If you have torn or ruptured your anterior cruciate ligament, or you are recovering from ACL reconstruction surgery, you are probably looking for physiotherapy close to home that you can get to regularly. Searching for ACL rehab physiotherapy near me usually means you want someone who understands the long, staged work of rebuilding knee movement, strength and control. We can introduce you to a UK physiotherapist who suits what you describe, and they will quote you directly.
need_heading: What people searching for ACL rehab physiotherapy usually need
need_lead: ACL rehabilitation is a gradual process, and the right physiotherapist for you depends on where you are in it.
needs: You have recently injured your knee and want to know whether your ACL is involved and what to do next.
You are preparing for or have just had ACL reconstruction and need help with swelling, movement and early exercises.
You are several months into rehab and want strength testing to guide whether you are ready for running, jumping or sport.
You are recovering from an ACL injury that is being managed without surgery and want to build knee stability.
You want a physiotherapist you can reach easily for regular appointments over many months of rehabilitation.
context_heading: Checking who is qualified to guide your ACL rehab
context: "Physiotherapist" and "physical therapist" are protected titles in the UK. Anyone using them must be registered with the Health and Care Professions Council (HCPC), and you can check the HCPC register online. Most physiotherapists are also members of the Chartered Society of Physiotherapy, shown by the letters MCSP.

Sports therapists, massage therapists and personal trainers can be helpful for some needs, but they are not physiotherapists. For an injury or post-surgery rehabilitation, check that you are booking an HCPC-registered physiotherapist.
tell_heading: What to tell us when you enquire
tell: Say whether your ACL injury was recent, whether you have had reconstruction surgery, or whether you are being managed without surgery.
Mention how far along your rehabilitation you are and what you can do now, such as walking, cycling or climbing stairs.
Describe any swelling, stiffness or giving way in the knee, and anything your surgeon or GP has advised.
Explain what you are working towards, whether that is everyday confidence, returning to running or a particular sport.
Give the area you can travel to for appointments, since regular visits over many months matter.
Note any other injuries, conditions or commitments that affect how often you can attend.
questions: Are you registered with the HCPC, and what is your experience of ACL rehabilitation?
How will you assess my knee and track my progress over the months ahead?
Will you use strength testing to guide when I can progress to running or sport?
What should I do at home between appointments, and how often will we go over it?
How do you work with surgeons or GPs if my knee needs further attention?
What are your fees, and how will you quote me for a course of rehabilitation?

faqs.q: Can ACL injuries be managed without surgery?
faqs.a: Some ACL injuries are managed without surgery, with rehabilitation to build strength and control around the knee. Whether that suits you depends on your injury, your knee and your goals, and a physiotherapist or surgeon can advise on your situation.

faqs.q: How long does ACL rehabilitation take?
faqs.a: ACL rehabilitation often takes many months, and return to sport usually takes many months too. Your physiotherapist can explain what progress looks like at each stage for you.

faqs.q: Why does strength testing matter in ACL rehab?
faqs.a: Strength testing helps guide progression, showing whether your knee is ready for the next stage of rehabilitation. It gives you and your physiotherapist something concrete to base decisions on rather than guesswork.

faqs.q: How do I check a physiotherapist is properly registered?
faqs.a: "Physiotherapist" is a protected title, so anyone using it must be registered with the Health and Care Professions Council (HCPC). You can check the HCPC register online before you book.
